name: Gettysburg Battlefield
significance: Turning point of the Civil War
description: Site of the bloodiest battle of the American Civil War and President Lincoln's Gettysburg Address.

name: Appomattox Court House
significance: End of the Civil War
description: Location where General Robert E. Lee surrendered to General Ulysses S. Grant, effectively ending the Civil War.

name: Fort Sumter
significance: Beginning of the Civil War
description: Site of the first battle of the American Civil War.

name: Antietam Battlefield
significance: Led to the Emancipation Proclamation
description: Site of the bloodiest single-day battle in American history.

name: Vicksburg Battlefield
significance: Split the Confederacy in two
description: Site of the Union siege that gave the North control of the Mississippi River.

name: Shiloh Battlefield
significance: First major battle in the West
description: Site of one of the earliest and bloodiest battles in the Western Theater.

name: Chickamauga Battlefield
significance: Greatest Confederate victory in the Western Theater
description: Major battle fought in northwestern Georgia, one of the most significant Union defeats.

name: Fredericksburg Battlefield
significance: One of the most one-sided Confederate victories
description: Union assault on Confederate positions resulted in severe Union casualties.

name: Chancellorsville Battlefield
significance: Lee's greatest victory, but lost Stonewall Jackson
description: Confederate victory where General Stonewall Jackson was mortally wounded by friendly fire.

name: Bull Run (Manassas)
significance: Site of two major Confederate victories
description: Location of the first major land battle and a second major battle, both Confederate victories.

name: Petersburg Battlefield
significance: Led to the fall of Richmond and Lee's surrender
description: Nine-month siege that eventually forced the evacuation of Richmond and Confederate surrender.

name: Spotsylvania Court House
significance: Brutal combat including the Bloody Angle
description: Two weeks of intense fighting as part of Grant's Overland Campaign.

name: Stones River Battlefield
significance: Secured central Tennessee for the Union
description: Tactically inconclusive but strategic Union victory near Murfreesboro, Tennessee.

name: Fort Donelson
significance: First major Union victory, opened Tennessee
description: Grant's victory that earned him the nickname 'Unconditional Surrender' Grant.

name: Kennesaw Mountain
significance: Part of Atlanta Campaign
description: Failed Union frontal assault during Sherman's advance on Atlanta.

name: Battle of Franklin
significance: Devastating Confederate defeat known as the 'Pickett's Charge of the West'
description: A massive frontal assault by Confederate Gen. Hood against entrenched Union forces, resulting in the loss of fourteen Confederate generals.

name: Battle of Cold Harbor
significance: One of American history's most lopsided battles
description: A defensive victory for Lee where Union forces suffered thousands of casualties in a hopeless frontal assault ordered by Grant.

name: Battle of the Wilderness
significance: First battle of Grant's Overland Campaign
description: An inconclusive but bloody battle fought in dense brush that neutralized Union artillery superiority.

name: Battle of Atlanta
significance: Decisive Union victory sealing the fate of Atlanta
description: General Sherman's forces defeated Confederate attacks, paving the way for the March to the Sea and Lincoln's reelection.

name: Battle of Nashville
significance: Destruction of the Army of Tennessee
description: One of the most decisive tactical victories for the Union, effectively ending the war in Tennessee.

name: Battle of Pea Ridge
significance: Secured Missouri for the Union
description: One of the few battles where Confederate forces outnumbered Union troops but were still defeated.

name: Battle of Wilson's Creek
significance: First major battle west of the Mississippi
description: A Confederate victory that focused national attention on the war in Missouri.

name: Battle of Glorieta Pass
significance: The 'Gettysburg of the West'
description: Union forces stopped the Confederate invasion of New Mexico Territory, preserving the West for the Union.

name: Battle of Mobile Bay
significance: Closed the last major Confederate port on the Gulf
description: Famous for Admiral Farragut's order, 'Damn the torpedoes! Full speed ahead!'

name: Bentonville Battlefield
significance: Largest battle fought in North Carolina
description: The last full-scale offensive by the Confederate army under General Joseph E. Johnston against Sherman.

name: Battle of Mansfield
significance: Thwarted the Union Red River Campaign
description: A Confederate victory that saved Shreveport and prolonged the war in the Trans-Mississippi theater.

name: Battle of Brandy Station
significance: Largest cavalry battle of the Civil War
description: Marked the emergence of the Union cavalry as a formidable fighting force.

name: Battle of Cedar Creek
significance: Ended Confederate resistance in the Shenandoah Valley
description: Union General Sheridan rallied his troops from a near-rout to a crushing victory.

name: Battle of New Market
significance: Famed for the charge of the VMI Cadets
description: Confederate victory where young cadets from the Virginia Military Institute were called into battle.

name: Battle of Monocacy
significance: The 'Battle That Saved Washington'
description: A tactical defeat for the Union that succeeded in delaying Early's march on Washington D.C.

name: Battle of Perryville
significance: Strategic Union victory securing Kentucky
description: The largest battle fought in Kentucky, ending the Confederate Heartland Offensive.

name: Andersonville Prison
significance: Most notorious Confederate military prison
description: Site where nearly 13,000 Union prisoners died from disease, malnutrition, and exposure.

name: Harpers Ferry
significance: Largest surrender of U.S. troops until WWII
description: Strategic armory town captured by Stonewall Jackson just prior to Antietam.

name: Battle of Seven Pines (Fair Oaks)
significance: Ended the Union advance on Richmond; J.E. Johnston wounded, replaced by Robert E. Lee
description: Fought just miles from Richmond, this inconclusive battle marked the beginning of Robert E. Lee's command.

name: Battle of Malvern Hill
significance: Final battle of the Seven Days Battles
description: Union artillery decimated Confederate infantry charges on this plateau, ending the Peninsula Campaign.

name: Battle of Gaines' Mill
significance: Lee's first major victory of the Seven Days
description: The bloodiest of the Seven Days Battles, breaking the Union line north of the Chickahominy River.

name: Battle of Cold Harbor
significance: One of American history's most lopsided battles
description: A defensive victory for Lee where Union forces suffered thousands of casualties in a hopeless frontal assault ordered by Grant.

name: Battle of the Wilderness
significance: First battle of Grant's Overland Campaign
description: An inconclusive but bloody battle fought in dense brush that neutralized Union artillery superiority.

name: Battle of North Anna
significance: Lee's 'Inverted V' trap
description: Lee outmaneuvered Grant, splitting the Union army, but was too ill to spring the trap.

name: Battle of Yellow Tavern
significance: Death of J.E.B. Stuart
description: Union cavalry under Sheridan defeated Confederate cavalry, resulting in the mortal wounding of J.E.B. Stuart.

name: Battle of Five Forks
significance: The 'Waterloo of the Confederacy'
description: Sheridan turned Lee's flank, forcing the evacuation of Petersburg and Richmond the next day.

name: Battle of Sayler's Creek
significance: Destruction of Lee's rear guard
description: Union forces captured nearly a quarter of Lee's retreating army just days before the surrender at Appomattox.

name: Battle of Ball's Bluff
significance: Early Union disaster leading to the Joint Committee on the Conduct of the War
description: A humiliating Union defeat on the Potomac River where Senator Edward Baker was killed.

name: Battle of South Mountain
significance: Prelude to Antietam
description: Union forces fought through three mountain gaps to catch Lee's divided army.

name: Battle of Lookout Mountain
significance: The 'Battle Above the Clouds'
description: Union forces swept the Confederates off the mountain slopes, opening the way for the assault on Missionary Ridge.

name: Battle of Missionary Ridge
significance: Broke the Siege of Chattanooga
description: A miraculous frontal charge by Union troops without orders that routed the Confederate army.

name: Battle of Fort Sanders
significance: Decisive Union victory in Knoxville Campaign
description: Longstreet's assault on the Union fort in Knoxville failed miserably with heavy casualties.

name: Battle of Franklin
significance: Devastating Confederate defeat known as the 'Pickett's Charge of the West'
description: A massive frontal assault by Confederate Gen. Hood against entrenched Union forces, resulting in the loss of six Confederate generals.

name: Battle of Nashville
significance: Destruction of the Army of Tennessee
description: One of the most decisive tactical victories for the Union, effectively ending the war in Tennessee.

name: Battle of Champion Hill
significance: Decisive battle of the Vicksburg Campaign
description: Grant defeated Pemberton's main army, forcing them to retreat into the defenses of Vicksburg.

name: Battle of Port Gibson
significance: Secured Grant's beachhead in Mississippi
description: The first engagement of Grant's march on Vicksburg, proving his army could operate on the east bank.

name: Battle of Corinth (Second)
significance: Secured the railroad hub for the Union
description: A failed Confederate attempt to retake the vital rail junction at Corinth, Mississippi.

name: Battle of Iuka
significance: Grant's first major battle in Mississippi
description: A sharp fight where Rosecrans defeated Confederate forces under Sterling Price.

name: Battle of Resaca
significance: First major battle of the Atlanta Campaign
description: Sherman and Johnston engaged in a heavy battle before Sherman flunked the Confederate line.

name: Battle of Pickett's Mill
significance: A bloody Union repulse
description: Sherman attempted a flank attack that ran headlong into entrenched Confederates in dense ravines.

name: Battle of Peachtree Creek
significance: First major attack by John Bell Hood
description: Hood attacked Thomas's army as it crossed the creek but was repulsed with heavy losses.

name: Battle of Atlanta
significance: Decisive blow to Confederate defense of the city
description: The largest battle of the campaign; Hood attacked Sherman's flank but failed to crush the Army of the Tennessee.

name: Battle of Jonesborough
significance: Fall of Atlanta
description: Sherman cut the last rail line into Atlanta, forcing Hood to evacuate the city.

name: Battle of Pea Ridge
significance: Secured Missouri for the Union
description: Union forces defeated a larger Confederate army including Native American troops, ending major Confederate offensives in Missouri.

name: Battle of Westport
significance: The 'Gettysburg of the West'
description: The largest battle west of the Mississippi, ending Price's Raid and Confederate hopes in Missouri.

name: Battle of Pilot Knob (Fort Davidson)
significance: A bloody assault on a Union earthwork
description: Outnumbered Union troops held off repeated Confederate assaults before blowing up their magazine and escaping.

name: Battle of Port Hudson
significance: Last Confederate stronghold on the Mississippi
description: The longest siege in US military history (48 days), noted for the participation of African American troops.

name: Battle of Mansfield
significance: Stopped the Red River Campaign
description: A Confederate rout of Union forces that saved Shreveport and Texas from invasion.

name: Battle of Sabine Pass II
significance: Most lopsided victory of the war
description: 46 Confederate artillerists held off a Union invasion fleet of 5,000 men and 4 gunboats.

name: Battle of Fort Fisher
significance: Closed the last major Confederate port (Wilmington)
description: The largest amphibious operation of the war, resulting in the capture of the 'Gibraltar of the South'.

name: Battle of Bentonville
significance: Last major battle of the war
description: Joseph E. Johnston's final attempt to stop Sherman's advance through North Carolina.

name: Battle of Olustee
significance: Largest battle in Florida
description: A sharp Confederate victory that prevented the Union from severing Florida's supply lines.

name: Battle of Glorieta Pass
significance: Ended Confederate invasion of New Mexico
description: Union forces destroyed the Confederate supply train, forcing a retreat back to Texas.

name: Battle of Palmito Ranch
significance: Final land battle of the Civil War
description: Fought on the banks of the Rio Grande more than a month after Lee's surrender; a Confederate victory.
